# US offers $15 million reward over IRGC drone network

A poster released by the US State Department's Reward for Justice program, July 30, 2026



The United States has offered a reward of up to $15 million for information that disrupts the financial mechanisms of Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), focusing on a company Washington says plays a key role in producing drones used by Tehran and its regional allies.

The State Department's Rewards for Justice program announced Thursday that it was seeking information on Kimia Part Sivan Company (KIPAS), which it described as the drone-production arm of the IRGC's overseas Qods Force.

According to the statement, KIPAS has conducted unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) flight tests for the IRGC-Qods Force, provided technical assistance for drones transferred to Iraq for use in IRGC operations, and procured critical UAV components from companies outside Iran.

Washington also named six senior KIPAS officials—Hasan Arambunezhad, Abolfazl Ramazanzadeh Moshkani, Mehdi Ghaffari Naghneh, Reza Nahar Dani, Abbas Sartaji and Hadi Jamshidi Zavaraki—saying they had been involved in the testing, development and supply of drones, particularly for Iranian-aligned armed groups in Iraq, Yemen and Syria.

The officials were sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury Department in April 2024 for acting on behalf of the IRGC-Qods Force, while KIPAS itself was designated in 2021 under U.S. counterterrorism authorities for providing material support to the organizatio

It has been a summer of good news for Ukraine.

Its drone strikes deep inside Russia have created gasoline shortages, strained Russia’s economy, stoked anxiety among ordinary Russians, and created headaches for Vladimir Putin. Ukrainian forces have effectively isolated occupied Crimea from the Russian mainland, and they continue to strike Russian vessels in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

But Russia has scored some points of its own recently, and not just by terrorizing Ukrainian civilians with long-range missiles. Agricultural products account for 60% of the country’s goods exports, and Russia’s attacks come just as Ukraine’s farmers prepare for the harvest season.

# Fears of wheat price surge amid Ukraine-Russia clashes in the Black Sea

Issued on: 31/07/2026 - 23:20

Intensifying clashes between Ukraine and Russia in the Black Sea are threatening a crucial trade artery responsible for nearly a third of the world's wheat supply, stoking fears of soaring prices and shortages.

![Smoke rises from the grain carrier Golden Leo after Russian missile strike in the Black Sea close to Odesa, Ukraine, 19 July 2026.](https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/afa92442-844b-11f1-9ca2-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26200564414743.jpg)

Earlier in July, a Russian cruise missile struck the grain carrier *Golden Leo*, claiming ten lives. This marked the deadliest blow yet in a mounting campaign by both Russian and Ukrainian forces targeting cargo ships in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

# The Caspian Sea is in turmoil: When the world's two biggest wars find a point of intersection.

### From a period of peaceful "strategic calm" lasting over a century, the Caspian Sea, the world's largest inland lake, is suddenly transforming into one of the planet's most dangerous hotspots. At this crossroads of Asia and Europe, the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the flames of the Middle East are in danger of merging into one, igniting consequences beyond control.

![Báo Thanh Hóa](https://vphoto.vietnam.vn/thumb/24x24/vietnam/resource/IMAGE/2025/1/21/a1e6a410511a4f6bb5ec6a186a706e85)Báo Thanh Hóa•31/07/2026

---

Ukraine's recent attack on an [Iranian](/en/tag/iran "Iran") ship in the Caspian Sea has raised concerns that Russia's war in Ukraine and its conflict in the Middle East are becoming increasingly intertwined. Photo: Bankingnews.

The fact that US President Donald Trump hosted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and [Ukrainian](/en/tag/ukraine "Ukraine") President Volodymyr Zelensky in Washington on the same day clearly reflects the current geopolitical reality. Two crises once seen as separate are increasingly showing signs of connection, and the Caspian Sea is where this intersection is most evident.

For many years, the Russia-Ukraine conflict has primarily revolved around the Black Sea, while the Iran-Israel tensions have been centered in the Middle East. These two conflicts exist in different strategic spaces, with distinct actors and objectives.
